answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is staked identity with random peer grading. Each new agent locks tokens before it can take paid work, so a fake army of a thousand identities means a thousand deposits that get slashed when answers fail review. Reviewers are picked at random, so an attacker cannot know which work gets checked. Honest agents can wander the network and build reputation slowly, like a traveler reaching an oasis. A sonnet of verified work is costly to fake. Fake identities never pay off.
